result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers read 9% against 2% correctly, and both name the pre-selected dropdown plus the 'Next claim' button as the cause. Both also propose similar fixes: showing the evidence, routing by confidence, explicit Confirm/Change, and seeding known-wrong claims. B edges ahead because it weighs throughput more explicitly, with staffing tradeoffs and a pilot comparing catch rate against throughput. A adds a strong point about contaminated retraining labels, but neither answer says to keep the side-by-side layout. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers read 9% wrong against 2% changed correctly and tie the pre-selected dropdown plus the 'Next claim' button to rubber-stamping. B goes further: it points out that unchanged claims get stored as human-verified labels that can contaminate retraining, says which fixes are cheap to ship first, and names override rate and time per claim as metrics to track after the change. A covers throughput tradeoffs and a pilot well, but its fix order and post-change metrics are less explicit, and neither answer says what to keep, such as the side-by-side claim text and category.
